name: Single-Agent Checkpoint Inhibitor (Dostarlimab or Pembrolizumab) for dMMR/MSI-H Endometrial Carcinoma
histology: endometrial carcinoma, mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability high (MSI-H)

biomarkers.note: Single agent PD-1 checkpoint blockade (dostarlimab or pembrolizumab) is the biomarker directed option for mismatch repair DEFICIENT (dMMR) or microsatellite instability high (MSI-H) advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma. pMMR disease is instead treated with lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab (see gyn-endometrial-pembro-lenvatinib). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Uterine Neoplasms v3.2026, ENDO-D 2 of 6 and ENDO-D 3 of 6 (MSI-H/dMMR tumors: Pembrolizumab; Dostarlimab-gxly). DeVita 12th ed. lines 175357 to 175375 establish that in MSI-H or dMMR advanced endometrial cancer the PD-1 inhibitors dostarlimab and pembrolizumab have activity.

lineOfTherapy: biomarker directed single agent immunotherapy for dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma; option after prior therapy

eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, ENDO-D 2 of 6 and ENDO-D 3 of 6 (MSI-H/dMMR tumors: Pembrolizumab; Dostarlimab-gxly)

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: line 233347 (pembrolizumab flat dose of 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks); dMMR/MSI-H endometrial activity lines 175357 to 175375

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., line 233347. Pembrolizumab flat 200 mg IV every 3 weeks (source stated alternative 400 mg every 6 weeks), given up to the source stated 2 year ceiling. Single agent option for dMMR/MSI-H disease. Manage immune related adverse events per checkpoint inhibitor toxicity guidance.

drugs.name: Dostarlimab-gxly

provenance.locator: ENDO-D 2 of 6 and ENDO-D 3 of 6 (MSI-H/dMMR tumors: Dostarlimab-gxly) - regimen identity only; per drug flat mg and schedule not printed on this page

drugs.notes: VERIFY: dostarlimab is a category equivalent single agent option for dMMR/MSI-H disease per NCCN Uterine v3.2026 ENDO-D, and DeVita 12th ed. (lines 175357 to 175375) confirms its activity in dMMR/MSI-H endometrial cancer, but neither licensed source prints the per dose flat mg or the induction/maintenance schedule (commonly a fixed dose every 3 weeks then every 6 weeks). basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are VERIFY and must be resolved from the drug label / study protocol before this protocol leaves DRAFT. Do not invent.

regimen.cycles: continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity; pembrolizumab up to the source stated 2 year ceiling. Pembrolizumab and dostarlimab are alternative single agents; only one is given per patient.
supportiveCare: immune related adverse event monitoring for either checkpoint inhibitor (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, endocrinopathies).

monitoring: immune related toxicity screen (endocrine, GI, pulmonary) at each visit

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold the checkpoint inhibitor and manage with corticosteroids per immune related adverse event guidance; clinical review before rechallenge.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 175357 to 175375 (PD-1 inhibitors dostarlimab and pembrolizumab active in MSI-H/dMMR advanced endometrial cancer); line 233347 (pembrolizumab flat 200 mg every 3 weeks)

guideline.locator: Systemic Therapy for Endometrial Carcinoma, Biomarker-directed therapy, MSI-H/dMMR tumors: Pembrolizumab; Dostarlimab-gxly (ENDO-D 2 of 6 and ENDO-D 3 of 6)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for single agent PD-1 checkpoint blockade (dostarlimab or pembrolizumab) in mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma (StewardMD reference disease endometrial cancer, subtype group #43). The pembrolizumab flat dose (200 mg IV every 3 weeks, source stated alternative 400 mg every 6 weeks) is grounded to DeVita 12th ed. line 233347; DeVita lines 175357 to 175375 establish PD-1 inhibitor activity in dMMR/MSI-H endometrial cancer. The dostarlimab per dose flat mg and schedule are set to VERIFY: neither the licensed core (DeVita) nor the guideline (NCCN Uterine v3.2026 ENDO-D, which names dostarlimab without printing the mg) establishes them, and they must not be invented. Biomarker gate (dMMR/MSI-H) is per NCCN Uterine v3.2026 ENDO-D 2 of 6 and 3 of 6. Pembrolizumab and dostarlimab are alternative single agents. verifyFields records the unresolved dostarlimab dose fields, which block status ACTIVE. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
